open.recommended_reason: Every string the app must mirror verbatim — the two mock permission alerts and the nine how-to labels — is already vy, so one register covers the whole widgets how-to screen an editor reads in one pass.
open.note: Keys: every app-owned line with a finite second-person verb or a possessive, including the 177 en units carrying a second-person possessive and the reader-predicate keys (achievements.streak.body, achievements.badge.hired.earned, onboarding.age.title, onboarding.personalGoal.title, focusTask.alert.deleteTask.message, screenTime.restrictedAppsPicker.deleteAlertMessagePrefix), plus onboarding.widgets.howTo.placeTitle and moneyfesting.details.stopConfirmationMessage (idiom proposals with a finite ty verb — 'Umísti si ho, kam chceš.' / 'vrať se s čistou hlavou' — that need a vy alternative too), plus the control role Retry.in_sentence. Rule: app-owned copy uses one address throughout, while a string that mirrors an iOS label or alert follows the device regardless (references/locale-briefs/cs.md '## Platform terms'). Evidence for vy: iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: UserNotificationsServer.framework | Localizable.strings | USER_NOTIFICATION_PERMISSION_ALERT_TITLE ('vám chce posílat'); FamilyControlsAuthenticationUI.app | Localizable.strings | NOTIFICATION_AUTH_REQUEST_MESSAGE_INDIVIDUAL ('povolíte', 'vaší aktivitě'); HealthUI.framework | HealthUI-Localizable.strings | AUTHORIZATION_DONT_ALLOW_ALERT_MESSAGE ('můžete'); and l10n.cz Stylistická příručka, https://l10n.cz/wiki/Slovníky/Stylistická_příručka/ fetched 2026-09-16: 'Pro oslovení uživatele používejte vykání („zadejte“, nikoliv „zadej“).' Evidence for ty: Apple's own Czech coaching copy in the same genre, ActivityUI.framework | Localizable.strings | THOPHY_CASE_ACTIVITY ('Uzavři svoje kroužky') and FitnessUIAssets.bundle/ActivityAchievements/MonthlyAchievements/localization/challenge/MoveStreak_SMALL_INCREASE | Localizable.stringsdict | ACHIEVEMENT_UNACHIEVED_ALERT_DESCRIPTION ('To dáš!'), plus the app's Romanian precedent of informal tu. Neither option has a shipped key: 0 cs copy exists. Buttons do not change either way, because the Czech control form is the infinitive. Meanwhile: agents write person-free forms wherever the meaning allows (infinitive buttons, nominal headers, impersonal neuter states, present tense with the pronoun dropped) and use vy where a finite second-person verb is unavoidable, so a flip to ty touches a countable list the adjudicator reports rather than the whole batch.

open.recommended_reason: It is the everyday Czech word a reader without English understands at first read, and the overlap with Apple's Focus mode is exactly the overlap en already accepts by calling both things Focus.
open.note: Keys: moneyfesting.details.*, focusTask.*, widgets.startFocus.*, widgets.focusRing.*, profile.home.focusSection, onboarding.dailyFocusGoal.* and every a11y label naming a session. Rule: one word per concept across the catalog; a flip is a global term change with its own follow-up batch, never a per-string choice. Evidence: 0 cs keys for either option. iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime names the system Focus mode Soustředění (Applications/Preferences.app | Localizable.strings | Focus; System/Library/ControlCenter/Bundles/FocusUIModule.bundle | Localizable.strings | MODULE_DEFAULT_TITLE), so the app's own focus word would share the noun; no en key names the system mode (en inventory 'Focus mode (system) (0), none found') and the app ships no Focus filter, so nothing forces the two to be told apart. 'fokus' is an English loan that reads as jargon and gives no natural adjective for 'focused hours'. The exact overlap to weigh is the bare label profile.home.focusSection (en 'Focus'), which is also the name of an iOS Settings row. Meanwhile: the first batch writes 'soustředění' and the adjudicator lists every key that touched the term.

open.recommended_reason: The workplace frame is what makes 'your hours have a price' legible without ever saying the app pays anyone, and the Czech shift-and-payroll vocabulary is everyday speech.
open.note: Keys: the 24 achievements.badge.*.name keys, the 5 achievements.category.*.name keys and the earned lines in BadgeCopy+{Comeback,FullDays,Payroll,Shift,Wages}.swift. Rule: the conceit is decided once per locale and every badge follows it; unlock criteria stay literal. Option 1, workplace event nouns: Příchod (Clocked in), Nástup (Hired), Na výplatě (Salaried), Návrat (Rehired), Na dobu neurčitou (Permanent), Odpracované roky (Tenure), Celá směna (Full shift), Dlouhá směna (Long shift), Dvojitá směna (Double shift), Zpátky na směně (Back on shift), Výplaty (Payroll), Směna (The Shift) — naming the event rather than the person is what keeps them gender-neutral, because Czech has no neutral personal noun for any of these; Salaried was reseeded from 'Výplatní páska' (a physical payslip, an object) to 'Na výplatě' (being on payroll, an event/state) so it matches the other badges' grammar instead of naming a document. Option 2, plain achievement nouns (První sezení, Týden v kuse, Dvacet ze třiceti): neutral by construction but it loses the reason the app prices time like work. Evidence: 0 cs keys for either; iOS 26.1 ships no Apple label for any of these, so both option sets are agent proposals. The option strings are the two strategies, so term_audit's option counts stay 0 until copy ships and the count column is not the signal here. Meanwhile: the first badge batch writes the event nouns listed in references/locale-briefs/cs.md '## Idioms and figurative language', marks each as a proposal, and the adjudicator lists every badge key that touched the conceit so a flip stays one scope.
